newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta unveils plans for alternative to VAT.
newsitem.headline: Malta unveils plans for alternative to VAT.

text.p: Maltese Finance Minister Lino Spiteri on Thursday launched a "white paper" outlining the government's plans for replacing Value Added Tax with a new system of customs and excise duties.

Speaking at a news conference to launch a draft proposal, Spiteri said VAT would be converted into an import duty of 15 percent on imports from the European Union, which make up some 80 percent of Malta's imports.
The government will introduce a five percent excise tax (ETP) on imported and locally produced goods, excluding exports. The tax will be collected by distributors.
A tax of five percent will be charged on pre-booked tourist accommodation and catering and there will be a 10 percent tax on business services and services given to the public.
Spiteri said retailers would no longer collect taxes for the government, with tax collected at one stage from distributors.

VAT was introduced in 1995 by the former Nationalist government at a uniform rate of 15 percent but the Labour Party made its removal a central plank of its electoral campaign, blaming it for a rise in the cost of living.
